title: BECE Business Studies: Book-keeping - Business Studies - Trial Balance
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A list of debit and credit balances extracted from the ledger at a particular date is known as a:
questions.explain: A **trial balance** is an internal accounting schedule that lists all the debit and credit balances extracted from the various ledger accounts on a specific date.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The primary purpose of preparing a trial balance is to:
options: determine the net profit for the year
check the arithmetical accuracy of the ledgers
calculate the value of closing stock
questions.explain: The primary **use of a trial balance** is to verify the arithmetical accuracy of the double-entry system. If the total debits equal the total credits, it is assumed that the ledger accounts are arithmetically correct.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The following are uses of a trial balance EXCEPT:
options: facilitating the preparation of final accounts
revealing all types of accounting errors
proving the arithmetical accuracy of double entry
showing a summary of all ledger balances
questions.explain: A trial balance does **not** reveal all errors. For example, errors of omission (completely forgetting to record a transaction) or errors of principle (entering an asset as an expense) will not prevent the trial balance from balancing.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In a trial balance, which of the following accounts will normally have a debit balance?
questions.explain: By the rules of double entry, **Purchases** represent an expense or asset acquisition and therefore carry a debit balance. *Capital*, *Sales*, and *Discount Received* are equity/revenue items and always carry credit balances.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All the following balances are recorded on the credit side of a trial balance EXCEPT:
questions.explain: **Debtors** are people who owe money to the business; therefore, they represent an asset. Assets carry debit balances. Liabilities (Bank loan, Creditors) and Equity (Capital) carry credit balances.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A ledger account shows total debits of $₦15,000$ and total credits of $₦10,000$. How is this extracted balance recorded in the trial balance?
questions.explain:
The balance is the difference between the heavier side and the lighter side.
$$₦15,000 \text{ (Debit)} - ₦10,000 \text{ (Credit)} = ₦5,000$$
Because the debit side is heavier, it results in a **debit balance of ₦5,000**, which is placed in the debit column of the trial balance.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q:
Calculate the correct total of the trial balance from the following extracted balances:

*   Capital $₦10,000$
*   Cash $₦4,000$
*   Purchases $₦8,000$
*   Sales $₦12,000$
*   Creditors $₦5,000$
*   Debtors $₦15,000$
questions.explain:
Sort the balances into Debit and Credit columns according to accounting rules:

| Item | Debit (₦) | Credit (₦) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Capital | | 10,000 |
| Cash (Asset) | 4,000 | |
| Purchases (Expense) | 8,000 | |
| Sales (Revenue) | | 12,000 |
| Creditors (Liability) | | 5,000 |
| Debtors (Asset) | 15,000 | |
| **Total** | **27,000** | **27,000** |
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An extracted trial balance has total debits of $₦42,000$ and total credits of $₦45,000$. To make the trial balance agree temporarily, what amount must be placed in a Suspense Account and on which side?
questions.explain:
A Suspense Account is used to artificially balance a trial balance until errors are found. 
$$₦45,000 \text{ (Credits)} - ₦42,000 \text{ (Debits)} = ₦3,000$$
The debit side is short by $₦3,000$. Therefore, **₦3,000 is placed on the debit side** to make both sides equal $₦45,000$.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When a ledger account is balanced, the 'balance b/d' (brought down) appears on the credit side. When forming the trial balance, this amount will be transferred to the:
options: debit side of the trial balance
credit side of the trial balance
questions.explain: The 'balance brought down' (`balance b/d`) defines the actual nature of the account. A `balance b/d` on the credit side signifies a **credit balance**, and thus, it must be recorded in the **credit side of the trial balance**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following items located on a trial balance is specifically a Balance Sheet item?
questions.explain: **Motor vehicle** is a fixed asset and therefore belongs in the Balance Sheet. *Rent paid*, *Discount allowed*, and *Purchases* are expense items and are transferred to the Trading, Profit and Loss Account.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q:
Consider the following items extracted from a trial balance:
I. Wages $₦2,000$
II. Fixtures $₦5,000$
III. Bank overdraft $₦1,500$
IV. Sales $₦8,000$

Which of these are Balance Sheet items?
questions.explain:
Balance Sheet items are Assets, Liabilities, and Capital. 
*   **Fixtures** (Asset) = Balance Sheet
*   **Bank overdraft** (Liability) = Balance Sheet
*   *Wages* (Expense) and *Sales* (Revenue) go to the Profit & Loss Account.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business has the following balances in its trial balance: Capital $₦20,000$ and Drawings $₦2,000$. How will these be treated when preparing the Balance Sheet?
options: Add Capital to Liabilities and Drawings to Assets
questions.explain: **Drawings** represent money or goods taken out of the business by the owner for personal use. In the Balance Sheet, it is treated as a reduction in owner's equity, so it must be **subtracted from Capital**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q:
A trial balance contains the following balances:
*   Machinery: $₦15,000$
*   Cash: $₦3,000$
*   Sales: $₦20,000$
*   Purchases: $₦12,000$
*   Capital: $₦10,000$

Calculate the total value of assets to be identified for the Balance Sheet.
questions.explain:
From the list provided, identify only the **Asset** accounts:
1.  **Machinery** (Fixed Asset) = $₦15,000$
2.  **Cash** (Current Asset) = $₦3,000$

$$\text{Total Assets} = ₦15,000 + ₦3,000 = ₦18,000$$

*(Note: Sales and Purchases go to the Trading Account; Capital is Equity).*
questions.subject: Business Studies
